title: Changing agency policy and reliance interests
shortTitle: Changing agency policy and reliance interests
summary: An agency changing policy must acknowledge the change, explain its reasons, and address contrary prior findings and serious reliance when they matter.
notes:
Fox permits policy change without a categorical requirement to prove the new policy superior in court. The agency must nevertheless account for the circumstances of change: its own contrary factual findings and serious reliance on its prior position can require a fuller explanation. Regents applies that principle even where an earlier memorandum disclaimed substantive rights; the disclaimer bears on the strength of reliance and does not excuse failing to consider it.

The notes distinguish several inquiries. Political supervision can influence policy within the statutory mandate, while pressure to consider forbidden factors remains problematic. Constitutional review remains available independently of APA reason-giving, as the later Fox fair-notice decision illustrates. Whether a court is assessing an agency’s process or reweighing its policy can be difficult at the boundary; the editors present that institutional concern without discarding the legal obligation to provide reasons.
